clue.text: Fine rain put an end to foremost of matches — it's sad

parts.note: to scotch a plan or rumour is to put an end to it

indicators.note: the foremost letter of a word is its first one, taken from matches

parts.note: its first letter is used

indicators.note: sad in the sense of sorry or wretched, so the letters of it's are knocked into a poor new order

parts.note: its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone gloomy that a drizzly day has ended the leading football matches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put an end to' is the verb sense of scotch, as in scotching a rumour, not the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Scotch mist is a thick drizzling mist, the soaking fine rain typical of the Scottish hills.

clue.text: Bird is soaring above hide

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits above the second
in a down clue, soaring means the word is reads upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: an animal's hide is its skin

explanation.surface: A bird flies high over a birdwatcher's hide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soaring' turns IS upwards to SI, which goes above SKIN; 'hide' looks like a birdwatching shelter but means skin.
explanation.definitionFit: The siskin is a small yellow-green finch common in European woodland.

clue.text: Duty of female in charge, leader of expedition

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, taken from expedition

parts.note: its first letter is used

explanation.surface: The job of a woman who heads an expedition.
explanation.definitionFit: An office is a position with its duties, as in the office of mayor, so the word means a duty or function.

clue.text: Politician more angry about seat

indicators.note: about means around, so the first word is placed around the second

parts.note: crosser means angrier
a bench is a long seat

explanation.surface: A politician becomes angrier in a row over where to sit.
explanation.walkthrough: A crossbencher sits in the British House of Lords without belonging to any party.
explanation.definitionFit: A crossbencher is an independent member of the House of Lords, a parliamentarian aligned with no party.

clue.text: Pal's winning move in game

definitions.meaning: second meaning: checkmate in chess, the move that wins

explanation.walkthrough: The 's is read as 'is', joining the two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A mate is a friend, and in chess mate (short for checkmate) is the winning move.

clue.text: Dalmatian seen on track

parts.note: spotted means seen
to dog someone is to track or follow them

explanation.surface: A Dalmatian is noticed on a running track or railway line.
explanation.definitionFit: A Dalmatian is the classic spotted dog, white with black markings.

clue.text: Male whale — it may be the target on board

definitions.text: it may be the target on board
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the bullseye at the centre of a dartboard

explanation.walkthrough: 'board' is a dartboard, whose centre is the bull.
explanation.definitionFit: Male whales, like male elephants and cattle, are called bulls; the bull is also a dartboard's central target.

clue.text: All that is poetry written after college

indicators.note: the poetry word is written after the college word

parts.note: uni is short for university, a college
verse is poetry

explanation.surface: Every poem penned after leaving university.
explanation.definitionFit: The universe is the whole of existence, everything there is.

clue.text: Beginning to like receiving tuition

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, taken from like

parts.note: its first letter is used
earning means receiving pay

explanation.surface: Someone starting to enjoy the lessons they are getting.
explanation.definitionFit: Learning is the acquiring of knowledge through study, which is what tuition provides.

clue.text: Post info to ground? Here's an easier alternative

indicators.note: ground as in crushed or milled, so these letters are broken up and reformed

parts.note: the letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Sending information by post to the ground floor is the simpler choice.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft option is the easy choice, the path requiring least effort.

clue.text: Head of security entering by way of official pass

indicators.note: the letter goes into the middle of the other word

parts.note: via means by way of

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, taken from security

parts.note: its first letter is used

explanation.surface: A security chief enters a country with an official permit.
explanation.definitionFit: A visa is an official endorsement in a passport allowing entry to a country.

clue.text: Conveyance for soldiers arrives in Rio — copter, possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters could be arranged another way

parts.note: ARR is the timetable abbreviation for arrives
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A helicopter arriving in Rio de Janeiro might be bringing troops.
explanation.walkthrough: ARR plus RIO and COPTER are rearranged together.
explanation.definitionFit: A troop carrier is a vehicle or aircraft built to transport soldiers.

clue.text: As a precaution, I name patient

parts.note: a doctor's patient is a case

explanation.surface: Someone names a patient just to be safe.
explanation.definitionFit: In case, used adverbially, means as a safeguard against something that might happen.

clue.text: Tons stored by operator, supplier of caviar

indicators.note: the letter is kept inside the other word

parts.note: a surgeon operates on patients

explanation.surface: A machine operator stores tons of caviar from a supplier.
explanation.definitionFit: Caviar is the salted roe of the sturgeon, a large fish.

clue.text: Accompany each other to match

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to go somewhere together
second meaning: to suit or harmonise

explanation.definitionFit: Things that go together suit one another, and people who go together travel as companions.

clue.text: Support company in housing American relative

parts.note: to second a motion is to support it

indicators.note: housing means containing, so the pair holds the other piece

explanation.surface: A firm backing an American at home sounds like a family business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is not a link here: it joins 'company' as the pair that does the housing.
explanation.definitionFit: A second cousin is a kinsman sharing a great-grandparent, a family member.

clue.text: Academic in atelier with us

indicators.note: with puts the second word straight after the first

parts.note: an atelier is an artist's studio

explanation.surface: An academic joins us in the artist's workroom.
explanation.definitionFit: Studious and academic both describe someone devoted to study and books.

clue.text: Compliant, old criminal about to perish

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first pair goes round the second piece

parts.note: bent is slang for crooked or criminal
to die is to perish

explanation.surface: An elderly convict on the verge of death has become docile.
explanation.definitionFit: Obedient means doing as one is told, the same as submissive or compliant.

clue.text: Condor, say, kept in this — shag too?

definitions.text: Condor, say, kept in this — shag too?

parts.words: Condor, say, kept in this — shag too?
parts.note: Condor is a brand of pipe tobacco and shag is coarse-cut tobacco, not birds as the surface suggests

explanation.walkthrough: Condor and shag look like birds (a shag is a cormorant), but both are kinds of pipe tobacco, so the container is not a cage.
explanation.definitionFit: A tobacco pouch is a small bag for carrying loose pipe tobacco such as shag.

clue.text: Engine part — offer to enclose information

indicators.note: the first word encloses the second

parts.note: a bid is an offer at auction
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: A mechanic offers to include details about a car component.
explanation.definitionFit: The big end is the larger end of a connecting rod, attached to the crankshaft in an engine.

clue.text: Modest order husband put in

indicators.note: the letter is placed inside the other word

parts.note: a caste is a social order or class

explanation.surface: A demure wife has her husband ordered in.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaste means pure and restrained in conduct, a sense close to modest or decent.

clue.text: The German taking in stranger, one who is slightly feeble

indicators.note: the first word takes the second inside it

parts.note: der is a German word for the
odder means stranger

explanation.surface: A German admits a stranger who is somewhat frail.
explanation.definitionFit: A dodderer is someone who totters or shakes with age, a frail and weak person.

clue.text: Apparition produced by artist with pens

indicators.note: pens as a verb means encloses, so the word holds the other piece

parts.note: taken as written
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A ghost drawn by a painter equipped with pens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pens' looks like a noun for drawing but is the verb for shutting in.
explanation.definitionFit: A wraith is a ghost or spectral figure, an apparition.

clue.text: Exhibit female pig swallowing hard

indicators.note: swallowing means taking the letter inside

parts.note: a sow is a female pig
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A sow eating something tough at an agricultural fair.
explanation.definitionFit: To show something is to display or exhibit it.

clue.text: Too much on top

explanation.definitionFit: Over means excessive (overdone) and also positioned above something.

clue.text: Hires these, animated for film

indicators.note: animated means lively, stirred up, so the letters move into a new order

parts.note: the letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A studio hires these people for an animated feature.
explanation.walkthrough: The Heiress is a 1949 film starring Olivia de Havilland.
explanation.definitionFit: The Heiress is a 1949 William Wyler movie, adapted from Henry James's Washington Square.

clue.text: Location shown in news item

indicators.note: the letters are on show inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across these two words

explanation.surface: A news story reveals where something happened.
explanation.definitionFit: A site is a place or position where something is located.

clue.text: To tie game, one may have been deployed in defence

definitions.text: one may have been deployed in defence

parts.note: a tie is a drawn match, a draw
bridge is a card game

explanation.surface: A sporting side tries to draw by playing defensively.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawbridge could be raised over a castle moat to keep attackers out.
